preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= m <= n <= 3000 for n, m in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, 1 <= m <= n <= 3000.

preconditions.expression: all(all(0 <= b <= 10**9 for b in bs) and all(0 <= w <= 10**9 for w in ws) for _, _, bs, ws, _ in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, all bee counts b_i and wasp counts w_i are non-negative integers up to 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges) for _, n, _, _, edges in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each test case provides exactly n-1 edges forming a tree on nodes 1 to n.
The sum of n over all test cases is at most 10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(int(line), int) for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is a valid integer.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(output_lines[i]) <= m for i, (_, m, _, _, _) in enumerate(test_cases))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output integer is between 0 and m inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(int(output_lines[i]) == max_wins(test_cases[i]) for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output equals the maximum number of villages Ugly Wasp can win in an optimal partition into m villages, where a village wins for Ugly Wasp if the sum of wasps in it is strictly greater than the sum of bees.
